postings.title: Finance Director
postings.description:
About Codat

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.

The Role

We're looking for a Finance Director to lead our finance team at Codat. You'll own the numbers from start to finish: the plan, the monthly close, the board pack and the conversations with our investors.

This is both a hands-on role and a senior role. You'll have one direct report and still do plenty yourself: one day you'll be taking the board through the forecast, and the next you'll be sorting out a payroll query or approving expenses. You'll report to the Chief Legal and Business Officer and work closely with the leadership team on where we spend money and why, and you'll be the person who tells us when the numbers don't support a plan.

What You'll Work On

 - Budgeting, forecasting and cash. You'll build the annual and longer-range plan with budget holders across the business, keep the forecast current and track how we're doing against it. You’ll also own cash flow forecasting and runway, plus headcount planning with the people team.

 - Board and investor reporting. You'll prepare the board pack, covering ARR, unit economics and customer metrics, and the analysis investors and advisers need.

 - The month-end close, management accounts and statutory consolidation across our UK and US entities, including intercompany. You'll also run the annual audit to sign-off and own our technical accounting positions, such as revenue recognition and share-based payments.

 - Group tax and compliance across the UK and US, and our relationships with auditors, tax advisers, lawyers and banks.

 - ARR and revenue modelling. You’ll partner with the team to ensure our commercial reporting keeps pace as the business evolves, covering the impact of product and pricing changes, and the bridge from ARR to recognised revenue. You’ll also work with the commercial team on pricing and contract terms, and what they mean for revenue recognition and billing. 

 - Day-to-day finance operations: You’ll work alongside our Senior Finance Manager on AP, AR, billing, payroll and expenses, and share the operational load rather than just overseeing it.  , The finance systems stack. We want finance to need less manual work every quarter, and automation and AI tools are part of how we'll get there.

 - A small finance team. You'll set their priorities and help them grow.

You'll Probably Have

 - A professional accounting qualification: ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent.

 - Held a senior finance role at a fast-growing, VC-backed tech or SaaS business, ideally across more than one entity and country. You've sat in board meetings and answered investors' questions yourself.

 - Experience in international tax compliance or managing tax advisers across jurisdictions.

 - A good grasp of SaaS metrics and revenue recognition, and the ability to explain them to people outside finance.

 - Stayed close to the detailed work as you got more senior. You're as comfortable building a model as you are closing the books.

 - The confidence to challenge senior people when the numbers call for it. If the data says a plan won't work, you'll say so.

 - Experience managing a small team and helping them grow.

 - AI is already built into how you work. You’ve used automation and AI to change how a finance function runs, not just to speed up the odd task. You can show us a process or system you’ve rebuilt and what it changed for the team. 

How We Work

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather make a sound decision quickly and adjust it than wait for perfect information. What you own is yours from start to finish.

We operate hybrid working but without strict mandates on how many days. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would.

postings.title: Senior AI Engineer
postings.description:
About Codat

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.


THE ROLE

Some of the biggest commercial banks in the world already work with us. Their relationship managers would rather spend time with clients than dig through the books to find out what's changed. We're building this for them.

We're building the Advisory Intelligence Platform. It puts Codat's client intelligence inside the assistant a banker already uses, starting with Microsoft Copilot. A banker can ask it anything about a client and get an answer from that client's actual books. If they don't ask, it tells them anyway when something important changes, and suggests what to do.

It's a senior role and a hands-on one. Bankers make real decisions based on what the assistant says, so impressing people in a demo isn't enough. It has to be right. Codat is AI-first, not AI bolted onto SaaS, and we work that way ourselves, with agents handling the repetitive work so engineers can focus on the hard problems. You'll build what you design and look after it once it's live, and you'll have a real say in where we take it.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - The reasoning layer. What goes into the model's context, which tools it calls, and when it should break a question into steps. Every number it gives has to trace back to a source, and it needs to know when to say it doesn't know. That last part is harder than it sounds.

 - Evals. You'll build the eval sets and harness, and do the analysis that tells us whether a change made the assistant better or just different. When a banker corrects an answer, that correction becomes a new test case.

 - Model choice and token economics. Which model should handle which job, and what that costs us per answer. Caching or a smaller model is often enough. For some questions a banker needs the strongest model available, and that's worth paying for.

 - The semantic and signal layers. You'll work on both with the data engineers. That means the definitions the model is allowed to use, and the signals that spot when something changes for a client. How the model uses them is down to you.

 - The agents and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers behind the assistant. This covers the tools the assistant can call, including the ones that will eventually let it draft that email. You'll work out how they break, and add the tracing we need to see what happened inside an answer.

 - Classical modelling where it beats an LLM. Anomaly detection, peer benchmarks, classifiers. Sometimes the best answer is a simple statistical model, not an LLM.


YOU'LL PROBABLY HAVE

 - Shipped LLM features that people actually used, and been the person they came to when something broke. You've designed how a model works with tools or structured data, and there are things you'd do differently now.

 - Built evals for your own work, and probably had one mislead you. We'd like to hear what you changed.

 - A feel for numbers, whether that comes from a quantitative degree or from your work. You want the denominator before you believe a percentage, and you notice when a headline figure is really about the mix of the data.

 - Opinions about models that come from using them. You've chosen between models on how well they did and what they cost, and you know when a classical model would do a better job.

 - Good engineering habits in Python or another general-purpose language. That means tested, modular services rather than notebooks. Strong SQL as well, and some experience with CI/CD, Docker, cloud (we're on Azure) and tracing for LLM systems.

 - Led work without having the title. People followed an approach you set because you made the case with evidence, and you can explain the trade-offs to someone who isn't technical.

 - AI as part of how you work, for research and prototyping as well as code.

 - Useful, not essential: fintech, lending or accounting; Spark or Databricks; semantic layers or metric views; fine-tuning.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We're more interested in what you've built and how you knew it worked than in a perfect match.




HOW WE WORK

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather ship something useful and improve it than polish it in private. What you build is yours from start to finish.

There's no return-to-office mandate, and you can work hybrid or fully remote. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would. What we don't want is anyone staying online late to prove a point.

postings.title: Software Engineer (Data)
postings.description:
About Codat

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.


THE ROLE

Some of the biggest commercial banks in the world already work with us. Their relationship managers want to spend their time with clients, not digging through the books to find out what's changed. We're building the thing that does the digging for them.

It's called the Advisory Intelligence Platform. It puts Codat's client intelligence inside the assistant a banker already uses, starting with Microsoft Copilot. Ask it anything about a client and it answers from that client's actual books. Don't ask, and it tells you anyway when something important changes.

Every one of those answers sits on data. Someone has to get that data in, shape it, define it and serve it, so the number the assistant quotes is the right one. That's you. You write production software, and you care about the data it moves as much as the code that moves it.

This role is for an engineer who's growing fast and wants room to grow faster. You'll ship from your first weeks, own what you build once it's live, and work alongside data and AI engineers who'll push you. Codat is AI-first, not AI bolted onto SaaS, and we work that way ourselves: agents take the repetitive work, engineers take the interesting problems.

 


WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - The data behind every answer. Services and pipelines that take raw data from accounting platforms, banks and payment systems and turn it into something a model can trust. When a source sends rubbish, your code notices.

 - The semantic layer. The definitions the model is allowed to use: what counts as revenue, when a month ends, which currency. Get it right and every answer agrees with every other answer.

 - The signal layer. Spotting when something changes for a client: a customer paying later, cash running tighter, a supplier quietly becoming critical. You'll help build the detection and make it fast and reliable.

 - The tools the assistant calls. MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and APIs that serve data to agents. You'll build them, test them and find out how they break before a banker does.

 - Keeping the numbers honest. Tests, data checks and observability that prove a number is right, and catch it the moment it isn't.


YOU'LL PROBABLY HAVE

 - Shipped production software that real people depended on, and written most of it yourself. Services, APIs or data systems with tests, not notebooks or config.

 - Had data be the hard part. A source that sent duplicates, a schema that changed under you, two teams who meant different things by "customer". You fixed it, and you'd design it differently now.

 - Good engineering habits in Python, C# or another general-purpose language. Tested, modular code the next person can change without fear.

 - An eye for SQL. You can read a query and tell whether it's right, whoever or whatever wrote it.

 - Stayed on the hook for something after it went live. You found out why it broke, fixed the cause, and added what would have caught it sooner.

 - Some time with CI/CD, Docker and cloud (we're on Azure). You've changed a pipeline, not just pushed to one.

 - A habit of asking why. If someone asks for a number the data can't support, you say so.

 - AI as part of how you work, and you can explain and defend what it helped you build.

 - Momentum. More ownership with each move, new stacks picked up quickly, things built that nobody asked for.

 - Useful, not essential: fintech, lending or accounting; Spark, Databricks or dbt; anything that puts data in front of an LLM.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We're more interested in what you've built and how fast you're growing than in a perfect match.

 


HOW WE WORK

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather ship something useful and improve it than polish it in private. What you build is yours from start to finish.

There's no return-to-office mandate, and you can work hybrid or fully remote. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would. What we don't want is anyone staying online late to prove a point.
